# Data layout

What each command does in full is in the [skills reference](../reference/skills.md). Words used here are in the [glossary](glossary.md).

## The tree

A layout that works without extra command-line tools:

```text
docs/system/
  _template/
  landscape.md       # short description, how the parts connect, v0 vs later, bulk A#s, feature index
  repos.md           # named repos (proposed until a URL exists), Synced at, Merges into and Work items go to per repo
  sweep-progress.md  # position of $crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs; not the source of truth (1.124.0)
  diagrams.md        # context diagram; $crav1-refresh-system-notes adds what is new
  glossary.md        # words the source already uses; not a feature spec
  security.md        # kept risks after $crav1-review-security (system pass); not seeded by spark
  adr/
docs/architecture/
  spec.md            # one architecture spec from $crav1-existing-to-specs
  left-out.md        # guesses that stay left out
docs/environments/
  marks.md           # confirmed environment lines from read-environment or map-pipeline-environments
docs/notes/
  index.md           # generated: one row per month
  YYYY-MM/           # month of the source date (1.61.0)
    index.md         # generated: one row per note
    YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md  # one full input (fact, dump, code change, meeting) and its source
    YYYY-MM-DD-pr-<repo>-<n>.md  # PR note: one per pull request, its title, description and PR record (1.65.0, 1.97.0)
docs/sources/
  YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/ # an imported mail, transcript, chat, screenshot, or other original
docs/research/
  <topic>.md         # research notes; a spec's ## Research findings links to them
docs/playbooks/
  <topic>.md         # a filled playbook copied on apply (1.120.0); the first write stays outside the project
docs/architecture/designs/
  <topic>/           # a design sandbox, one goal, on its own design branch (1.181.0); no other skill reads it except explain-tech, read-only, as not decided
    goal.md          # end goal, drivers, constraints, criteria
    compare.md       # designs in this topic scored against the shared criteria
    designs/<name>/  # design.md, questions.md, diagrams.md, adr/ drafts, stages.md once staged
  _compare/          # one-off cross-topic comparisons, only when asked
docs/data-model/
  <model>/
    index.md         # flow, scope, revision; scope confirmed only after a yes
    confirmed.md     # append-only Approved snapshots, one stage and revision each
    proposed.md      # recommendation, decisions, examples, diagrams, transition
    questions.md     # unanswered questions, with the specs they affect
    comparisons.md   # area view and platform view, neither the default
    sources.md       # pinned sources and the hash that was checked
    checkpoint.md    # written when an auto run stops unfinished
    reviews/         # immutable report.md and report.pdf snapshots
docs/specs/
  _template/
    spec.md          # what / why / acceptance
    plan.md          # how / constraints / files / linter
    tasks.md         # ordered, testable slices
    verify.md        # acceptance matrix after implementation
    fix-log.md       # one gap from verify-build-against-spec, fix + re-proof
    live-fix.md      # legacy; new incidents go in fix-log.md
    work-item.md     # optional Azure Boards id starter (comment only)
  <change-id>/
    spec.md
    plan.md
    tasks.md
    verify.md
    fix-log.md
    diagrams.md      # ideas-to-spec and tighten-spec
    adr/             # slice decisions
    export/          # EARS, BDD, OpenSpec, YAML, JSON, or BMAD copies
    notes.md         # optional, from ideas-to-spec
    explore.md       # bugs from $crav1-run-exploratory-test
    walk-progress.md # position of $crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build; not the source of truth
    build-progress/  # one file per work branch for $crav1-build-walk; not the source of truth
    claims.md        # In progress: lines so another session can see a walk (1.151.0)
    work-item.md     # Azure Boards ids, one per line
```

`$crav1-plan-from-spec` writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md` into that folder so teammates see them.

The host file names for the two rules are in [install](../install.md) and on the skill pages.

**Kit drop-in.** `$crav1-update-kit` replaces the installed kit on the current branch from a published release: `.cursor/skills/crav1/`, `.cursor/agents/crav1-*.md`, the `crav1-*` folders and `README.md` under `.cursor/agent-assets/`, `.cursor/rules/crav1.mdc`, and the Claude Code twins under `.claude/` (`crav1-*` skills, `crav1-docs`, `crav1-*` agents, `crav1-*` agent assets, and `CLAUDE.md`). A file already copied from `docs/specs/_template/` or `docs/system/_template/` is replaced only when it still matches the old kit apart from line endings. Kit files are compared the same way: CRLF and LF are not a local edit. Specs, `walk-progress.md`, `build-progress/`, `claims.md`, plans, tasks, notes, playbooks, the build map, and the rest of `docs/system/` are not part of that replace. that allow-list is the vendor table `vendors.json` in the update-kit skill. the kit repo holds generated copies under `vendors/codex/` and `vendors/copilot/`. Codex is part of the replace when `.crav1/kit.json` lists it (or, when that file is missing, when its marker file is present): `.agents/skills/crav1-*`, `.agents/skills/crav1-docs/`, and `agents/openai.yaml` on command-only skills. Copilot is still not part of the replace. `.crav1/flags.local.json` is an early-access flag file for this repo, written by `flags-on` and `flags-off`, and `.crav1/.gitignore` lists `flags.local.json`. The project's `.gitignore` is not changed. With no flag file, the replace matches 1.205.0. the commit stages the files the release ships. A skill or agent named `crav1-2-`, a `.crav1-2/` folder, and `sot/` are not part of that replace. The project's `AGENTS.md` is not written. a merge of two pristine installs of those copies is settled to the newer release by `kit_merge.py settle` in `$crav1-finalize-commit`, including a file the newer release adds or deletes. A copy that was edited by hand is left. the installed `crav1-docs/` folder is a compact edition of these pages, generated for the kit's skills. The pages in this repo stay the human edition. `llms.txt` at the kit repo root indexes them for outside tools. A held task in the ready check includes one whose only wait is an `(after:)` on a task that is not built yet, and the reason is on that held line.

## Notes

every `$crav1-add-to-spec` input (fact, dump, code change, meeting) becomes **one note** that holds the full input and its source. Each matching spec gets only its own short points, each followed by `Full source: docs/notes/YYYY-MM/<file>.md`. Notes are never absorbed; `used_by` grows as specs take points. There is no Note choice and no "never used" flag. The rule is `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/notes.md`.

Each note is `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`. The note also records `imported`. A source with no date is filed under the import date with `source_date: none`, and the run says so. The shape is `docs/notes/_template/note.md`:

```text
---
title: Title
kind: fact | dump | code change | meeting | email | chat | review-pr | pull request | converted spec
source: <mail subject, sender, sent date | meeting date and title | file path | commit sha | PR <n> <repo URL path>>
source_date: YYYY-MM-DD
imported: YYYY-MM-DD
source_folder: docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/
commits: []   # code change only (1.64.0)
pr_note:      # code change or review-pr from a pull request (1.65.0)
used_by: []
waiting_for: []
later_for: []   # saved for later on a spec, or general (1.195.0); written only when used
---
# Title

Source date: YYYY-MM-DD. Imported: YYYY-MM-DD.

<the full input, verbatim>
```

**Generated indexes.** `docs/notes/index.md` (one row per month) and `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/index.md` (title, date, kind, source, used by, waiting for) are built from the front matter by `notes_index.py` in the `crav1-add-to-spec` skill folder (`scripts/notes_index.py`). `--check` fails when an index is stale, so a product repo can run it in CI. No skill edits an index by hand. Lookups for a spec follow its `Full source:` links; matching new input and the duplicate check read the indexes.

**Duplicate check.** The same source again (the same mail, meeting date and title, file, or commit) is not written twice: the run says `already imported on <date> as <note>` and offers reuse (for specs that took nothing yet) or skip. The same point from a different source adds the new note as a second source on the existing spec line. A disagreement is written as a `**Conflict:**` line for the user to decide, never an overwrite; `$crav1-resolve-open-questions` settles it. a code change is also matched commit by commit: the note's `commits:` list (or its `source` expanded with git) and `git patch-id` for the same change under another SHA. Commits already imported are left out, and a fully imported change takes the reuse-or-skip path.

**Parked specs.** A parked spec gets nothing written; its slug goes in the note's `waiting_for` until `$crav1-retire-spec` un-parks it. `waiting_for` holds parked slugs only.

**Saved for later.** A meeting item saved for later adds a spec slug, or `general` for team-workflow information, to the note's `later_for`. Nothing is written into the spec. `$crav1-help`, `$crav1-tighten-spec`, `$crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions`, and `$crav1-retire-spec` list these notes as saved for later, never as waiting; `notes_index.py later --slug <slug>` lists them.

**Older notes.** Notes from before 1.61.0 (flat in `docs/notes/`, no front matter, maybe `Absorbed by`) are still read; `Absorbed by` counts as used by. To move them, run `notes_index.py migrate-dry-run` first by hand (prints planned moves, source fills, and link rewrites; writes nothing), then the one-time move, `notes_index.py migrate`. It files notes by source date, fills `source` and `source_folder` from each note's `Source:` lines and list items (1.63.0: `source_folder` is the first `docs/sources/` path, `source` that line; empty when there is none, never guessed; `$crav1-add-to-spec` uses these for its already-imported check), rebases every relative link inside a moved note (folders, any file type, anchors) and rewrites every markdown link to a moved note anywhere in the repo, anchors kept, with correct relative paths and lists each changed file, and rebuilds the indexes. Re-running is safe. Old spec lines keep their source lines; nothing is backfilled. `$crav1-bundle-to-specs`, `$crav1-ideas-to-spec`, `$crav1-spark-to-spec`, `$crav1-tighten-spec`, and `$crav1-existing-to-specs` add their slug to `used_by` when they quote a note; `$crav1-ado-sync`, `$crav1-help`, and `$crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` read the month folders and the generated indexes.

### PR note (1.65.0)

One note per pull request holds its title and description: `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-pr-<repo>-<n>.md`, filed by the pull request's created date, `kind: pull request`, keyed by `source: PR <n> <repo URL path>` (host, repo and number), so it is never written twice. The body names the URL, the author, base ← head and the state, then `## Description as of <date>` and the description after the personal-data and secrets check; images get the four options. When a later read finds a changed description, a new dated section is appended; earlier text is never removed. `$crav1-review-pr` writes or reuses it on every review, `$crav1-merge-pr` after a merge, and `$crav1-add-to-spec` for a code change from a pull request (or a branch with exactly one pull request on a signed-in host). `$crav1-open-pr` does not. A code-change note from that pull request carries `pr_note:` with its path. From 1.97.0 the PR note also holds the shared `## PR record` and the review history (below), and `$crav1-pr-status` writes it too.

### PR record (1.97.0)

The PR note's `## PR record` section, right after the header lines, is the one shared record of a pull request. `$crav1-pr-status`, `$crav1-review-pr`, `$crav1-add-to-spec` and `$crav1-merge-pr` read and write it. One line per item, kinds in this order: `- Order:` (a pull request it depends on, or that depends on it), `- Point:` (one point with its status: `done <sha>`, `agreed`, `declined`, `answered` (1.199.0: answered and accepted, no code change), `open`, `waiting on <name>`, `needs <name>`, `follow-up` or `migrated`), `- Read:` (what one person's last pr-status run saw; `Read: sweep` is the sweep watermark, not a person, 1.124.0), `- Ready:` (yes, no or merged, and why) and `- State:` (the host state). Lines are merge-safe: each sits in sorted place, a skill replaces only its own line where it is, and a Point is never deleted. After the record comes the dated history, each section word for word and never rewritten: `## Description as of`, `## PR updates as of`, `## Comment as drafted`, `## Comment as posted` (with a source line), `## Replies as drafted (not posted)`, whose heading `ado_threads.py reply --pr <n> --thread <id> --file <draft file> --note <PR note>` marks `thread <id> posted <date>` once that reply is posted. Review follow-ups are `follow-up` Points; `$crav1-ado-sync` reads them as open items. `$crav1-merge-pr` reads the `Ready` line. The full format, with made-up examples, is the add-to-spec reference `pr-record.md`. See [From a pull request's threads](../from-pr-status.md).

**Before 1.97.0** `$crav1-review-pr` kept follow-ups, `Asked on the PR:` questions, `(done in <sha>)` and `(Not in the posted comment, <date>; still open.)` marks and the comment history in a separate `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/review-pr-[<repo>-]<n>-follow-ups.md` (`kind: review-pr`). Such a note is still read, as `migrated` Points. `$crav1-add-to-spec migrate-formats` moves it into its PR note, keeping every line: one Point per bullet, the dated sections into the history by date, the intro and bullets under `## Review follow-ups, moved <date>`, then it deletes the old file and rewrites links to it. See [From a pull request review](../from-review-pr.md#comment-as-posted-1670).

## Sources

Each imported source is one folder, `docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/`. When the date is unknown, the folder is `docs/sources/undated-<slug>/`. The slug is short, lowercase, with hyphens, and never a person's name. The folder holds the original files and a `README.md`. The full convention is the add-to-spec reference [sources.md](../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/sources.md). The personal-data part is summarized in [Data policy](data-policy.md).

A quote in a spec from an imported source carries `Source: docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/`. Under `## Trace`, each pass adds one line: `Trace: docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/ — <what this pass marked new, already there, and inferred>.`

## Research and stale marks

On yes, it adds one blockquote below the note's title and owner line:

```text
> Stale since <date>: <one line on what changed>. Source: docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/
```

On each spec the quote was written into, or that links to that note, it adds under `## Research findings`:

```text
Stale since <date>: <one line>. See <note path>.
Point: <short label>. <the research line or the question, quoted>.
```

There is one `Point:` line per hit. When the note is updated, `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` or `$crav1-add-to-spec` checks each point and clears, narrows, or routes it. `$crav1-explain-existing-system`, `$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this`, and `$crav1-ado-sync` show a stale note as stale and do not clear it. The full rules are in [research-stale.md](../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/research-stale.md).

## Open question marks

Under each item in a spec's `## Open questions`, the kit can add four kinds of lines:

```text
- <question>
  - Pending: drafted <date> for <who>, <channel>. Not marked as sent yet. Question <n> of that draft.
  - Asked: <date>, <channel> to <who>. Question <n>. Date from <the user's yes | email <date> | meeting <date> | chat <date>>.
  - Answered: <date>, <who>, <kind>: "<quote>" Source: docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/
  - Blocks: T2, T4
```

`Blocks:` names the tasks that wait on a kept-open question, or `Blocks: none` when the question blocks no current task. A short reason may follow in parentheses: `Blocks: none (later phase)`. `$crav1-resolve-open-questions` writes a task list after a keep-open pick of tasks, and writes `Blocks: none` when the pick is None. The whole slice writes `Blocks: whole slice`. `$crav1-plan-from-spec` writes `Blocks: T#` for a question that blocks some current tasks, and `Blocks: none` for a leftover that blocks none. The risk line for `Blocks: T2, T4` is `kept open; blocks T2, T4 until resolved.` Only a question with no `Blocks:` line keeps "do not implement until resolved". a kept-open question with no `Blocks:` line holds the `T#` ids named in its text for [`$crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](../from-tasks-ready-to-build.md), and holds the whole slice only when no task is named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded. Any `Blocks:` line wins over a plan Risk that says do not implement until resolved. A risk matches on the question's first sentence, a `(question: <first words>)` tag, or the same Blocks tasks named in the risk. a task that waits on a held task is held too (`held, waits on T3`), and the ready check result is `ready`, `ready-partial`, or `not-ready`. the ready check groups those ready and held tasks by build-map branch and names each as `T#` plus its short name.

`$crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` writes `Pending:` or `Asked:` after you say whether the draft was sent. `$crav1-add-to-spec` write `Answered:` when a kept quote clearly answers that question. `$crav1-resolve-open-questions` then walks the question with you. The full format is in [open-questions.md](../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/open-questions.md).

## Approval needed

`## Approval needed` sits beside `## Open questions`.

```text
- The partner approves applying the CI build policy.
  - Person: the partner
  - Holds: T4
  - Approved: the partner, 2026-10-02, https://github.com/example/widgets/pull/12#discussion_r9, "Yes, apply the policy." (accepted by Alex 2026-11-12)
```

`Person:` is who gives the yes. `Holds:` is the tasks that wait. A matching `Approved:` line clears the hold and stays. `$crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` may write `Asked:` or `Pending:` under the item and never sends the draft.

## Readiness marks

[`$crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](../from-tasks-ready-to-build.md) reads these marks and does not write them. It rewrites `build-map.md` every run. the tighten-and-plan ready check prints a `Run next:` block first. the ready check, the tighten-and-plan walk, and `$crav1-build-walk` fetch the specs repo first; a copy that is behind origin stops and Run next is `git pull --no-rebase`. A claimed task is held `in progress by <user> since <date>` and is not offered in Run next.

- No `Reviewed:` line: the task can still be ready, with a warning to run `$crav1-review-plan`.
- No `(after: …)`: the task just before it blocks it while unticked (1.103.0; before, every earlier unticked task did).
- A kept-open question with no `Blocks:` line holds the `T#` ids named in its text, and holds the whole slice only when no task is named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded. `Blocks: none` blocks no task. A plan Risk that says do not implement until resolved blocks the whole slice when it matches no question, or matches a question with no `Blocks:` line. It matches on the question's first sentence, a `(question: <first words>)` tag, or the same Blocks tasks named in the risk. A `Blocks:` line wins.

A ticked task is Done only when `verify.md` lists it as verified. a ticked task that `verify.md` still lists as not implemented, a `Next:` line that names a ticked task, or a merged task that is still `Not implemented`, is not Needs verify. The ready check flags `verify.md` as behind and prints `Waiting: $crav1-verify-build-against-spec <slug> - verify.md is behind tasks.md (T2)`. It does not print a `Next:` line from `verify.md` that names a ticked task. A merged task whose status is `Implemented, verified, tick pending` is not behind. an older `Next:` line is stale only for a ticked task whose own row says Not implemented, claimed done or unverified, or has no row. A Verified or Failed row means verify is current, and verify no longer writes a `Next:` line. A verify-only change does not reopen the ready check and does not force `not-ready`. The walk and the ready check do not write `verify.md`. Only the walk's record or `clear --yes` restamps `walk-progress.md`.

## One spec, several branches (1.64.0)

The rules are in `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/branches.md`; the marks are in the tables below.

- **Where branches are named:** the `Synced at` slice lines (one per repo and branch, 1.84.0), the Match `Branch:` lines (one per branch, 1.86.0), and a task's `(branch: …)` part. Together, minus base branches and `(dropped)` entries, these are the spec's **work branches**.
- **Base branch:** the repo's `Merges into` cell in `docs/system/repos.md`, else the default branch. A branch diff starts at the **fork point** (where the branch split off), so a branch cut from `develop` in a repo whose default is `main` shows only its own commits, even before the `Merges into` cell is filled.
- **Same change after a rebase:** commits are matched by `git patch-id`; when an imported commit is gone from disk after a force push, the note's commit line (`<short sha> <author date> <subject>`) is matched instead.
- **Done across branches:** every work branch merged into its base (contained, the same change, or a merged PR on GitHub or Azure DevOps). A deleted branch whose work is in the base counts as merged. Report only: no skill writes `Status:` because of it.
- **Other repos:** code is read from the sibling checkout `../<repo>`, read-only. Refs on disk only; nothing fetches.

```text
docs/system/repos.md      | orders-api | … | develop | … |
                          ## Synced at
                          - orders-api develop@00344be, 2026-10-15
docs/specs/orders/spec.md   Synced at: orders-api develop@00344be, 2026-10-15
                            Synced at: orders-api feat/orders-retry@155b5c4, 2026-10-19
                            - Branch: feat/orders-retry
                            - Branch: feature/orders-openapi
docs/specs/orders/tasks.md  - [ ] T3: … (verify: unit — …) (spec: …) (after: T1) (branch: feat/orders-retry)
docs/notes/2026-10/…md      commits: [155b5c4, 2c0e1a9]
```

## Merge-safe formats (1.84.0)

These formats keep their additions on different lines, so git merges them cleanly most of the time; `$crav1-finalize-commit` resolves the rest by rule. The full rules are in `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/merge-safe.md`.

- **`Synced at`:** one line per repo and branch. In `spec.md`: `Synced at: <repo> <branch>@<short sha>, <date>`. In `docs/system/repos.md`: a `## Synced at` section after the table, `- <repo> <branch>@<short sha>, <date>`; the table has no `Synced at` column. A read replaces only its own line.
- **Match `Branch:`:** one line per branch, `- Branch: [<repo> ]<branch>` plus its markers; never `; `-joined.
- **Open questions:** `- ` bullets found by their words. `Q#` is shown, never written.
- **Sorted place:** a new `Synced at` or Match `Branch:` line (by repo, then branch), open question (by its words), `**New:**` line (by date, then text) or glossary row (by term) goes before the first existing one that sorts after it. Existing lines are never reordered. Appending always hits the same spot, the end, so two people's additions collide there; sorted places almost never coincide.
- **Migration:** a project made before 1.84.0 runs `$crav1-add-to-spec migrate-formats` once after updating, and again after 1.86.0 to split `; `-joined `Branch:` lists. It rewrites every `spec.md` and `repos.md` at once, keeps every line, checks nothing was lost before it writes, and a second run changes nothing.

## Work item homes

Each implementation repo has its own work item home: the Azure DevOps (ADO) project its work items go to. The home is the `Work items go to` cell for that repo in `docs/system/repos.md`:

```text
ADO: <org>/<project>
```

- The specs repo itself never has a home. Its cell stays empty.
- Skills that write `repos.md` add the column when it is missing and leave new cells empty. The first Azure Boards skill that needs a home asks once per repo, with the repo's own ADO project marked as the suggestion, and writes the cell after the answer. A later run reads the cell and does not ask again. To change a home, edit the row.
- A task goes to the home of the repo it touches. A Feature goes to the homes of its spec's repos: one Feature per home, each holding only its own repos' tasks. Features in the same org are linked as related. Features in different orgs mention each other in the description.
- `Jira: <project>` is reserved for later. Nothing reads or sends to Jira yet, so a repo with a `Jira:` cell is treated as having no home.

## Work item file

`docs/specs/<slug>/work-item.md` is optional and only for Azure Boards linking. One id per line, optionally with the milestone or slice it belongs to:

```text
Work item: 52 (ADO: contoso/orders)
Work item: 81 — October billing (ADO: contoso/orders)
```

Each id line ends with its [work item home](#work-item-homes), `(ADO: <org>/<project>)`. An older line without the tag is read as the org and project in `docs/environments/marks.md`, and the next skill that writes the file adds the tag.

The commit and pull request skills turn the id into a mention from the git remote: `#52` on Azure Repos, `AB#52` on GitHub. Leave the ids out of `tasks.md`. Task lines (`Work item: <id> — task: T<n> <title>`) record the child work items of the Feature. A task id is never the only mention. The template comment is [`docs/specs/_template/work-item.md`](../specs/_template/work-item.md).

## Spec sections the kit looks for

| Heading | Where | What reads or writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `## Acceptance criteria` | `spec.md` | Yes or no lines. Plan maps each to a task. Verify checks them |
| `## Open questions` | `spec.md` | Tighten-spec, resolve-open-questions, show-or-ask-open-questions; the marks above |
| `## Approval needed` | `spec.md` | Plan-from-spec and build-tasks add an item. Record-approval writes `Approved:`. Show-or-ask drafts the request. Resolve does not remove the item or an `Approved:` line |
| `## Assumptions`, `## Constraints` | `spec.md` | Written by intake and ideas; read by resolve-open-questions and plan |
| `## Repos` | `spec.md` | Written by intake for a one-repo feature |
| `## Match` | `spec.md` | Match status: done, partial, not in the code, or retired. Read by plan, tighten-spec, explain-existing-system, build-features |
| `## In the code` | `spec.md` | Paths of code that already exists. Plan and tighten-spec read that code first |
| `## Research findings` | `spec.md` | Links to `docs/research/` notes and stale marks |
| `## Trace` | `spec.md`, `plan.md` | Source trace lines on the spec; acceptance to task map on the plan |
| `## Security` | `spec.md` | Kept findings from `$crav1-review-security` on one spec |
| `## Dismissed test suggestions` | `spec.md` | Suggestions dismissed in `$crav1-suggest-tests-for-code`. Not acceptance and not a task |
| `## Linter` | `plan.md` | The linter or checker the build must leave green, or a line that there is none |
| `## Left as committed` | `plan.md` | Built pieces you chose to leave. Not offered again unless you say so |
| `## How the parts connect`, `## Feature index` | `docs/system/landscape.md` | The picture. Refresh-system-notes adds lines. Explain-existing-system compares them |
| `## Left out`, `## Dismissed` | `docs/architecture/left-out.md` | Existing-to-specs and read-environment |
| `used_by` | front matter of a note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` | Which specs took points from the note (older notes: `## Used by`) |

## Renamed skills (1.56.0)

The old names were removed in 1.58.0; the [renamed skills](../README.md#renamed-skills-1560) table maps each old name to the new one. A merged skill keeps each old skill's rules in `.cursor/skills/crav1/<skill>/branches/<id>/BRANCH.md`.
